title: Polynomial-Time Computability of the Link Decision
statement: There exist a finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet and natural numbers $C,c$ such that, for every Boolean word $z$, $M$ halts after exactly $C(|z|+1)^c$ steps with output the one-bit word whose bit is the tail-link decision for $z$.
replaced:
The single-bit tail-link decision on round requests is polynomial-time
computable, as a conjunction of two finite-word equality tests.
